This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice T.G. Shivashankare Gowda
 Oral Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioner apart from seeking enhancement of compensation, has challenged the dismissal of the claim against the Insurance Company vide judgment and award dated 30.05.2015 in M.V.C.No.2478/2018 passed by the XIII Addl. Small Cause Judge and Member, MACT, Bengaluru ('the Tribunal' for short).

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

Brief facts of the case are, on 29.04.2015 at about 12.30 p.m., while the petitioner was pedestrian at Kalasipalya private bus stop, a bus bearing No.KA-51 A- 9292 all of a sudden took reverse and dashed against the petitioner due to which she fell down and suffered injuries.
After taking treatment at Victoria Hospital, the petitioner has approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.

After taking the evidence and hearing both parties, the Tribunal by impugned judgment awarded compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-
with 9% interest p.a. and directed the owner of the bus to pay the compensation.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner is before this Court.
4. Heard the arguments of Sri.Karthik A.Bharghav, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Ravish Benni, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

5. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that inspite of medical records showing multiple NC: 2024:KHC:32439 fractures sustained by the petitioner, the compensation awarded is on the lower side.

The petitioner did not examine the medical officer and for this reason, the compensation awarded towards pain and suffering and loss of amenities and discomfort is insufficient and sought for enhancement.

SHIVAMMA AND ANOTHER' IN MFA No.6889/2011 wherein this Court ordered for pay and recovery and he sought for direction to the Insurance Company to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of the bus.
6.

entities.text: M/s. ICICI LOMBARD GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LTD. Vs. SHIVAMMA AND ANOTHER
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the compensation assessed by the Tribunal is based on the nature of injuries.
The NC: 2024:KHC:32439 petitioner has not explained the disability showing the injuries affecting her earning capacity.
Adequate compensation is awarded and it is not a case for enhancement of compensation.

6(a) It is further contended that the bus was not holding a valid permit at the time of accident and there was clear violation of the terms and conditions of the policy and to buttress his argument, he has relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'M.S. MIDDLE HIGH SCHOOL Vs. HDFC ERGO GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. AND OTHERS' reported in 2018 ACJ 2108.

entities.text: M.S. MIDDLE HIGH SCHOOL Vs. HDFC ERGO GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. AND OTHERS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. The material on record points out that there was an accident involving the bus and the petitioner.

The medical records show that the petitioner has suffered NC: 2024:KHC:32439 fracture of right wrist, fracture of distal end of radius, facture of stylid process of ulna and fracture of superior ramis of right pobrichae.
She was hospitalized from 29.04.2014 to 06.05.2014.
She was attended by an attendar and has spent money for travelling and other incidental expenses.
Petitioner undergone pain and suffering and loss of amenities and discomfort.
She needed four months to resume to working capacity.
The petitioner as a victim of accident is entitled to enhanced compensation.
9. The Tribunal awarded Rs.10,000/- towards medical expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards incidental expenses.
The same is reasonable and kept intact.

The petitioner having sustained multiple fractures, is entitled to Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomfort and loss of income for 4 months laid up period.
The accident is of the year 2014.

A person with no proof of income will earn not NC: 2024:KHC:32439 less than Rs.8,500/-
p.m.
Hence, loss of income comes to Rs.34,000/- and total compensation to Rs.1,49,000/-.

The Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- thereby enhancement of compensation is Rs.49,000/-.
10.
As regards liability is concerned, the Tribunal has exonerated the Insurance Company for the reason of violation of permit.
The material on record shows that at the time of accident, the bus was plied without permit.
Hence, there is clear violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
In SHIVAMMA's case, supra, the co-ordinate Bench of this Court discussed the liability on part of the Insurance Company and it is a clear case of violation of permit.

The judgment in M.S.MIDDLE HIGH SCHOOL, supra, the Hon'ble Apex Court has not referred to the facts of the said case so as to apply the principle that in case of violation of permit, the Insurance Company cannot be directed to pay compensation.

Since it is a case of violation of permit as held by the co-ordinate Bench of this Smt. Geetha vs Sri Chandrashekar C on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2750340/
3 Court in SHIVAMMA'S case, it is a case of pay and NC: 2024:KHC:32439 recovery.

sentences.text:
Hence, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed-in-part;
ii) Impugned judgment and award is modified;
iii) Petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.49,000/- against the award of the Tribunal.
iv) The owner of the bus is liable to pay the compensation.
v) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation of Rs.1,49,000/-
with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit, within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the judgment and to recover the same from the owner of the bus in the same proceedings.

SD/-
